updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to sell a single accessory to a walk-in customer for cash, so that the amount I ask them to pay matches the invoice on screen
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
In a Metro by T-Mobile store, most of a rep's day is spent activating phone lines and taking bill payments, and every one of those starts by looking up or creating a customer account. Accessory Sale is the short path for the customer who only wants to buy something off the shelf - a case, a charger, a screen protector - and walk out. There is no account to find, no phone number, no plan: the rep opens Accessory Sale, puts the items on the invoice, takes the money, and hands over a receipt. Behind the scenes the store books the sale against a shared walk-in account so it still shows up in the store's sales history, but the rep never sees or types a customer's details. This test walks the simplest and by far the most common version of that: one accessory, paid in cash. It is the case that proves the money is right - that the price the customer is charged is the item's price plus its tax, that the running invoice total matches, and that the payment screen asks for exactly that amount and no other.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2353 (Quick Sale - Accessory Only Sale), RTPL-2354 (Full Flow), RTPL-2355 (Add Accessories to Cart), RTPL-2356 (Payment Processing)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it. On a till with a paired tablet the customer is asked to approve the invoice on the tablet between the invoice and the payment screen; with no tablet the sale goes straight from the invoice to payment, and that is the path this test walks.
- The invoice is empty at the start - if a previous sale is still open on this till, cancel it before beginning.

## Test data
- **Accessory to sell:** Item number 101026, POPSOCKETS CEILING, $14.99, 4,321 on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), opened from the Browse accessories list; item detail panel read Price $14.99, Tax $1.50, Final price $16.49)_
- **Store:** Store EZLOGIC, dealer code 30247306  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), shown in the page header after sign-in)_
- **Cash to hand over:** $16.49 - the exact invoice total  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), the amount box opened pre-filled with 16.49 and the sale settled to a zero balance)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Add accessories** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-01-add-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Browse accessories list** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-02-browse-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Payment screen** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-04-payment.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Invoice paid in full** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-05-paid-in-full.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- This is the reference run for every other Accessory Sale test - the other tests reuse these opening steps and then branch.
- Step 3 is the empty-invoice guard: assert both that Continue reports itself unavailable and that clicking it does nothing. A button that looks greyed out but still navigates is the defect this check exists to catch.
- The amount the customer owes is always the item's price plus its tax; a mismatch between the item detail panel's Final price and the invoice Total due is a real defect, not a rounding quirk.
- If the accessory named in the test data no longer works when you run this - it has sold out, or it no longer appears in the list - pick the next well-stocked accessory from the Browse accessories list and read its own Price, Tax and Final price from the item detail panel before asserting any amount. If nothing in the list behaves as described here, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.
- To type a different cash amount, select the whole Amount box and type the full figure (for example 20.00). Deleting the box down to nothing makes it read 0.00 with the message Cash amount cannot be zero or more than $99,999. and greys out Collect amount; if that happens, reload the page to get the pre-filled amount back. (Seen live UAT3 2026-10-08.)

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want the screen to tell me the change owed when a customer hands over more cash than the invoice, and to let me hand the cash straight back if they change their mind
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Walk-in accessory customers usually pay in cash, and cash rarely matches the total to the penny - somebody buying a $16.49 phone grip hands over a twenty. The rep has to know, without doing the sum in their head at a busy counter, exactly how much change to take out of the drawer. Accessory Sale handles this by letting the rep type in what the customer actually handed over rather than only the amount owed, and then showing the difference back as change due. The same screen also has to cope with the customer changing their mind at the counter: the rep must be able to give the cash straight back and put the invoice back to unpaid, without cancelling the whole sale. This test covers both halves of handling cash at the counter - taking too much and giving it back - because both are moments where a store can lose real money if the screen shows the wrong figure.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2356 (Quick Sale - Payment Processing), RTPL-2730 (Refine Accessory Sale Flow - cash drawer)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it, so the sale goes straight from the invoice to the payment screen.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory to sell:** Item number 101026, POPSOCKETS CEILING, invoice total $16.49  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), item detail panel read Price $14.99, Tax $1.50, Final price $16.49)_
- **Cash the customer hands over:** $20.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), typed over the pre-filled amount; the screen then showed Change due back to customer $3.51)_
- **Change the rep owes back:** $3.51  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the invoice panel after collecting $20.00 against a $16.49 total)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Change due back to customer** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-06-change-due.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Payment screen** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-04-payment.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The change owed must equal the cash taken less the invoice total, to the penny. This is the figure the rep counts out of the drawer, so a wrong value here is a direct cash loss.
- Giving the cash back must return the balance to the full total and leave the invoice lines alone. If the items disappear along with the cash, that is a defect.
- If the accessory named in the test data no longer works when you run this, pick the next well-stocked accessory from the Browse accessories list, read its Final price from the item detail panel, and hand over a round sum comfortably above it - then expect change of that sum less the total. If nothing in the list behaves as described here, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.
- To type a different cash amount, select the whole Amount box and type the full figure (for example 20.00). Deleting the box down to nothing makes it read 0.00 with the message Cash amount cannot be zero or more than $99,999. and greys out Collect amount; if that happens, reload the page to get the pre-filled amount back. (Seen live UAT3 2026-10-08.)

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want two of the same accessory to bill as two separate lines that I can take off one at a time, so that the total always matches what is actually on the counter
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
A customer buying two identical phone grips is an everyday counter sale. Accessory Sale has no quantity box: each time the rep adds the item, it goes onto the invoice as its own separate line, so buying two of something produces two lines rather than one line reading 'x2'. That matters to the rep in two ways. First, the total must be the sum of every line, so two $16.49 lines must come to $32.98 and not to anything else. Second, when the customer changes their mind and only wants one after all, the rep must be able to take exactly one line off and see the total drop by exactly that line's amount, without clearing the whole invoice and starting again. This test proves both: that repeating an item stacks up correctly, and that removing one line leaves the rest of the sale intact.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2355 (Quick Sale - Add Accessories to Cart), RTPL-2734 (quantity behaviour in Quick Sale)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.
- The accessory used has at least two on hand, so adding it twice is within what the store actually holds.

## Test data
- **Accessory to sell twice:** Item number 101026, POPSOCKETS CEILING, $16.49 each including tax, 4,321 on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), added twice from the Browse accessories list; the invoice showed two lines of $16.49 and Total due $32.98)_
- **Expected total for two:** $32.98  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the invoice panel with both lines present)_
- **Expected total after removing one:** $16.49  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the invoice panel after Remove from invoice)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Invoice with two lines of the same accessory** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-03-cart-two-lines.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- Expect two distinct invoice lines after the second add - a single line whose amount has doubled would be a change in behaviour worth raising.
- Check the total after each add and after the removal, not only at the end; a total that is right at the end can still have been wrong in between.
- If the accessory named in the test data no longer works when you run this, pick the next well-stocked accessory from the Browse accessories list and read its Final price from the item detail panel before asserting any amount. If nothing in the list behaves as described here, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to put an accessory on the invoice by scanning or typing its item number, so that I do not have to hunt for it in a list at a busy counter
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
At a counter with a queue, a rep does not browse a list of seven thousand accessories - they point a barcode scanner at the packaging, or type the number printed on the label, and the item lands on the invoice. Accessory Sale offers this as the first of its two ways to add something: a Scan accessory item field that accepts the number and adds the item immediately, at its normal price, with no further clicks. It is the route most sales actually use, so it has to put exactly the same line on the invoice, at exactly the same price, as picking the item out of the list would. This test proves that the scan route works and bills identically to the browse route.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2355 (Quick Sale - Add Accessories to Cart)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory item number to enter:** 101026 (POPSOCKETS CEILING), $14.99 plus $1.50 tax, 4,321 on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), confirmed in the Browse accessories list and in the item detail panel)_
- **Expected invoice line and total:** POPSOCKETS CEILING $16.49, Total due $16.49  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), the same item added from the list produced this line and total)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Add accessories - scan entry** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-01-add-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The item goes on at its normal price with no confirmation step - if a panel opens asking the rep to confirm before adding, that is a change in behaviour worth raising.
- Compare the line amount against the same item added from the accessory list; the two routes must bill identically.
- If the item number named in the test data no longer works when you run this - the item has sold out, or is no longer stocked - take the item number of the best-stocked accessory from the Browse accessories list and use that instead. If no item number is accepted at all, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to be stopped with a clear message when I scan an accessory the store has none of, so that I never promise a customer something that is not on the shelf
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
A store's records and its shelves do not always agree, and an item number can still be scannable long after the last one has been sold. If Accessory Sale let the rep put such an item on the invoice, the customer would be charged for something the store cannot hand over, and the store's stock count would go negative. So the sale refuses any accessory the store has none of, and says so plainly, naming the item that was refused, rather than silently doing nothing. This test covers that refusal on the route where it matters most - the scan field, where the rep is going fast and may not notice a line quietly failing to appear.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2733 (out-of-stock items must be rejected in Quick Sale)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory the store has none of:** Item number 1003, HEAD PHONE CABEZA ATRAS ROJO, $35.00, no stock on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), its detail panel showed Qty 0 and offered no way to add it; scanning it produced the refusal message below)_
- **Expected refusal message:** Item out of stock - Item '1003' is out of stock and cannot be added to the invoice.  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), captured verbatim from the message that appeared after scanning item 1003)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Out of stock refusal** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-08-out-of-stock-toast.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The message appears briefly at the top right of the screen and clears itself, so capture it at the moment the item is refused rather than looking for it later.
- Check the invoice as well as the message - a refusal that still adds the line would be the more serious defect of the two.
- If the item number named in the test data starts working when you run this - the store has been restocked - sort the Browse accessories list by quantity smallest first and take the item number of any accessory showing no quantity. If every accessory in the list has stock, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want an accessory the store has none of to offer me no way of adding it when I open it from the list, so that I cannot put it on a customer's invoice by accident
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Refusing an out-of-stock accessory after the rep has already tried to add it is the safety net. The better outcome is that the rep is never offered the option in the first place. When an accessory the store has none of is opened from the accessory list, its detail panel still shows the rep what the item is and what it would cost - useful when a customer asks - but it offers no way to put it on the invoice at all: the add button simply is not there, and the only way out of the panel is to close it. This test proves that the guard is built into the screen and not only into the refusal message, so that a rep working quickly is stopped before they make the mistake rather than after.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2733 (out-of-stock items must not be selectable in Quick Sale)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory the store has none of:** Item number 1003, HEAD PHONE CABEZA ATRAS ROJO, $35.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), found by sorting the Browse accessories list by quantity smallest first; its detail panel showed Qty 0)_
- **Expected detail panel figures:** Price $35.00, Tax $3.50, Discount ($0.00), Final price $38.50  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the Item detail 1003 panel)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Browse accessories list** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-02-browse-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- The check that matters is the absence of the add button, not the presence of an error - assert that the panel offers Close and nothing else.
- The item detail figures should still be shown; a panel that hides the price entirely would be a different, unintended behaviour.
- If every accessory in the list has stock when you run this, or the item named in the test data has been restocked, sort by quantity smallest first and take whichever accessory shows an empty quantity. If none does, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to knock money off an accessory before I put it on the invoice, so that I can honour a price I have promised a customer without calling a manager
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Reps are often asked to come down on the price of an accessory - a customer buying a phone and a case together expects something off, or a manager has promised a walk-in a deal. Accessory Sale lets the rep do that at the counter, without anyone else's approval, as long as the new price stays inside a range the business sets per item: a floor the store will not sell below, and a ceiling which is the item's normal list price, since this is a discount and never a mark-up. The rep can express the same discount in whichever way the conversation went - the price they agreed, a percentage off, or a number of dollars off - and all three arrive at the same figure. The discount is measured from the item's list price, and tax is then charged on the reduced price, not the original one, so the customer is never taxed on money they did not pay. This test walks a rep applying a discount all three ways to the same accessory and then putting it on the invoice at the reduced price.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2788 (Price Adjustments for Cart Items - Quick Sale flow), RTPL-2965 (Accessory price adjustment in the Payment flow)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it, so the sale goes straight from the invoice to the payment screen.
- The invoice is empty at the start.
- THIS CASE NEEDS SEEDED DATA. It needs an accessory that is in stock, has a lowest allowed price below its list price, AND is approved for sale at this store. updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want the accessory list to show me only loose stock and never phones, so that I cannot sell a device through the accessory counter
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Accessory Sale exists for loose stock - cases, chargers, cables, screen protectors - the things a store counts by the boxful. Phones and other devices are different: each one is tracked individually by its own serial number, and selling one has to go through the proper activation or device sale flow so the right record is kept against the right handset. A device sold through the accessory counter would leave the store's device records wrong. To make that impossible rather than merely discouraged, the accessory list is locked to loose stock: the filter that restricts it is switched on and cannot be switched off, the option that would show everything is unavailable, and there is no option to show devices at all. This test proves the lock is real and not just a default the rep could undo. It also covers the ordering of the list, which is set to show the best-stocked items first so a rep is offered what the store actually has plenty of.

## Related tickets
RTPL-3063 (lock the inventory filter to non-serialized), RTPL-2989 (remove the Serialized filter and rename labels), RTPL-2733 (list the best-stocked items first)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Expected filter list:** Active (on), All Items (unavailable), Non-serialized (on and unavailable to switch off), Tangible (on), Non-tangible (unavailable). No Serialized option at all.  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the filter list on the Browse accessories screen)_
- **Expected list ordering:** Best-stocked accessories first - the top rows showed 4,321 then 3,451 then 577 on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), read from the Browse accessories list on opening, before any sorting was applied)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Accessory list filters** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-09-filters.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Browse accessories list** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-02-browse-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- Assert the exact set of choices offered, not just that Non-serialized is ticked - the absence of any device option is the real protection here.
- Assert that Non-serialized is both switched on and unavailable to change; a filter that is merely on by default could be undone by the rep and would not satisfy this rule.
- The list ordering can be changed by the rep by clicking a column heading - check the ordering on first opening the list, before touching any column.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want cancelling a sale to ask me why and remind me to hand back any money already taken, so that a customer never walks away out of pocket
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Sales fall through at the counter, and they most often fall through late - after the customer has already handed over their cash and then spotted the wrong colour, or changed their mind about the price. Cancelling at that point is the moment with the most risk in the whole flow: if the rep walks away without giving the money back, the customer is out of pocket and the store has taken cash for nothing. Accessory Sale handles this by never cancelling silently. It asks the rep to say why, spells out what cancelling will do - including that any money already taken has to be returned to the customer - and only then ends the sale and sends the rep back to the dashboard. This test walks that late cancellation, with cash already on the invoice, because that is the version that protects real money.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2355 (Quick Sale - cancel returns the rep to the main menu), RTPL-2353 (Quick Sale - Accessory Only Sale)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it, so the sale goes straight from the invoice to the payment screen.
- The invoice is empty at the start.

## Test data
- **Accessory to put on the invoice:** Item number 101026, POPSOCKETS CEILING, invoice total $16.49  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), item detail panel read Price $14.99, Tax $1.50, Final price $16.49)_
- **Cash to take before cancelling:** $16.49 - the exact invoice total  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), the amount box opened pre-filled with 16.49 and the sale settled to a zero balance)_
- **Reason to give for cancelling:** No issue to report  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08 (re-walked; first confirmed UAT3 2026-09-03), one of the three reasons offered in the cancel dialog)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Cancel transaction dialog** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-07-cancel-dialog.png` (attach from the run folder)
- **Payment screen** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-04-payment.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- Assert the reminder about returning tendered payments word for word - it is the line that protects the customer's cash and the reason this dialog exists.
- Cancelling is the right way to clean up after any of these tests, so this case doubles as the tidy-up routine.
- If the accessory named in the test data no longer works when you run this, pick the next well-stocked accessory from the Browse accessories list and read its Final price from the item detail panel before asserting any amount. If nothing in the list behaves as described here, contact the manual QA team to help get working data rather than staying blocked or hunting for data alone.

updates.name: As a Metro by T-Mobile authorized dealer, I want to be stopped when I try to sell an accessory below the store's floor price or above its list price, so that I cannot give away margin or overcharge a customer by mistyping
updates.custom_requirements:
## What this test is about
Letting a rep set their own price at the counter is only safe if there is a fence around it. The business sets a floor per accessory - the least the store is prepared to sell it for - and the ceiling is the item's ordinary list price, because this is a discount and a rep must never be able to charge a customer more than the shelf price. There is deliberately no manager override in this version: a price outside the range is simply refused, for everyone, with a message that names the limit that was breached so the rep knows what they are allowed to do. This matters in both directions. Below the floor the store loses margin on every sale, and a mistyped figure - a missing decimal point - could hand an accessory over for almost nothing. Above the ceiling the customer is overcharged. This test types a price just outside each end of the range and checks that both are refused and that neither reaches the invoice.

## Related tickets
RTPL-2788 (Price Adjustments for Cart Items - Quick Sale flow)

## Preconditions
- The rep is signed in at store EZLOGIC.
- The till has no customer tablet paired to it.
- The invoice is empty at the start.
- The accessory used has a price range set for it: SCREEN REPLACEMENT, list price $50.00, lowest allowed price $2.50. It has no description of its own, so its detail panel shows the words Item Not Found under its name - that is expected for this item and does not stop the test.

## Test data
- **Accessory to price:** SCREEN REPLACEMENT (shown in the Item number column, no description), list price $50.00, 577 on hand  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08, Browse accessories list and item detail panel: Price $50.00, Tax $5.00, Final price $55.00)_
- **Allowed range:** $2.50 MIN, $50.00 MAX  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08, Price adjustment section of the item detail panel)_
- **Price below the floor:** $2.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08, typed live - refused with Price below minimum value $2.50.)_
- **Price above the ceiling:** $51.00  _(verified: UAT3 2026-10-08, typed live - refused with Price above maximum value $50.00.)_

## Screens (design reference)
- **Item detail with the Price adjustment panel** — screenshot: `screens/quick-sale-02-browse-accessories.png` (attach from the run folder)

## Automation Notes
- Check both halves of each refusal: the message appears AND Add accessories is greyed out. A message that is shown while the item can still be added at the bad price is the defect this case exists to catch.
- Each message names the limit that was breached, so assert the amount in the text as well as the wording.
- Type into the Amount box key by key, as a person would. Setting the value directly without key presses leaves the panel unchanged and no message appears - that is the test tool, not the application.
- Do NOT click Add accessories on SCREEN REPLACEMENT at any point - this store refuses that item with the message SKU 'SCREEN REPLACEMENT' is not approved and cannot be added. Only approved accessories are allowed. That refusal is a different rule and not part of this test; this case never adds the item.
- There is no manager override in this version, so expect a flat refusal for every user and no approval prompt anywhere in the flow.
- If SCREEN REPLACEMENT no longer shows a range (MIN equal to MAX), or no longer appears in the list, do not hunt for another item alone: contact the manual QA team to get an accessory with a price range set for this store.
